name: Widget
description: The chrome round whatever a widget shows: a title bar, the states a panel fed by a request can be in, and — inside a `DashboardGrid` — the handles that move and resize it.

props.name: id
props.description: Which layout item this widget is. Left out, it is chrome with no place — a card.

props.name: name
props.description: What the widget is called where a control has to say so — the handles' labels and the announcements. Defaults to a string `title`, then to `id`.

props.name: description
props.description: A line under the title, for the question the widget answers rather than the noun it is named after.

props.name: actions
props.description: The end of the title bar: a menu, a filter, a link out.

props.name: level
props.description: The heading level the title renders at. Default `3`, since a dashboard is a section of a page.

props.name: loading
props.description: Bars where the content will be, and `aria-busy` while they are showing.

props.name: error
props.description: What went wrong, shown in place of the content. With `onRefresh` it comes with a retry.

props.name: empty
props.description: There is nothing to show: `true` for the default line, or the words to use instead.

props.name: onRefresh
props.description: Fetch it again. A button in the title bar, and the retry an error state offers.

props.name: refreshLabel
props.description: The refresh button's accessible name. Default `Refresh <name>`.

a11y: The title is a real heading at `level` (default `3`), so a dashboard has an outline rather than a page of anonymous boxes, and the widget is named by it.
`aria-busy` while it is loading, so a reader is told the panel is not finished rather than reading the skeleton out as content.
An error is a `role="status"`: it arrives after the page settled, and interrupting is for something the person did rather than something that failed on their behalf.
